interface.name: create_coupon
interface.title: Create Discount Coupon
interface.description: Creates ONE discount coupon in the store -- a percentage or fixed-amount code with an expiry date and optional spend, cap and redemption limits -- and returns the created coupon.
whenToUse: The merchant explicitly asks to create a discount code, e.g. 'create a 10% off coupon called SUMMER10 that expires at the end of August'.
The merchant explicitly asks for a fixed-amount discount, e.g. 'make a 50 SAR off code for orders over 300' -- set type to 'fixed', amount to 50 and minimumAmount to 300.
The merchant explicitly asks to cap a percentage discount, e.g. '15% off but never more than 100 SAR' -- set type 'percentage', amount 15 and maximumAmount 100.

The merchant explicitly asks for a coupon that starts later, e.g. 'set up an Eid code that begins next Friday' -- set startDate; the coupon is created immediately but customers cannot redeem it before that date.
The merchant explicitly asks to limit redemptions, e.g. 'only the first 100 customers' or 'one use per customer' -- set usageLimit and usageLimitPerUser.
whenNotToUse: The merchant wants to see, search or audit the coupons that already exist rather than add one -- use list_coupons instead.
The merchant named one existing coupon and wants its details, or wants to confirm a coupon this tool just created actually persisted -- use get_coupon with the id this tool returns.
The merchant wants to change, disable or extend a coupon that already exists -- this tool only creates new ones and cannot edit; use update_coupon instead.
The merchant wants a bulk campaign of many generated codes sharing one prefix (Salla's group coupons, is_group) -- this tool creates a single code; use create_group_coupon instead.
The merchant wants an affiliate or influencer coupon that tracks a marketer's sales (Salla's marketing coupons, marketing_active) -- use create_marketing_coupon instead.
The merchant is asking about promotional banners or store-wide offers rather than a redeemable code -- use list_special_offers instead.

code.description: The code customers type at checkout, e.g. 'SUMMER10'. Must be unique in the store -- Salla rejects a code that already exists, so check with list_coupons before creating one the merchant may already have.

type.description: How the discount is calculated: 'percentage' takes amount as a percentage off the order, 'fixed' takes amount off as a flat sum in the store's currency.

amount.description: The size of the discount: a percentage when type is 'percentage' (10 means 10% off), or a flat sum in the store's currency when type is 'fixed' (50 means 50 SAR off). Send a plain number here -- the created coupon reports it back as an {amount, currency} object.

expiryDate.description: The last day the coupon can be redeemed, as YYYY-MM-DD. Required by Salla: a coupon with no expiry cannot be created through this endpoint.

freeShipping.description: Whether redeeming the coupon also makes the order ship free. Required by Salla, so state it explicitly; false is the ordinary discount-only coupon.

excludeSaleProducts.description: Whether products already discounted in a sale are excluded from this coupon. Required by Salla. True stops the coupon stacking on top of sale prices, which is what a merchant usually means by 'not on items already reduced'.

startDate.description: The first day the coupon can be redeemed, as YYYY-MM-DD. Omit to make it usable immediately. A future date creates a scheduled coupon, which list_coupons reports with the 'not_started' status.

minimumAmount.description: The smallest order total, in the store's currency, that the coupon applies to -- 'on orders over 300'. Omit for no minimum.

maximumAmount.description: The largest discount the coupon may ever take off, in the store's currency. Mainly for percentage coupons, to stop a large order taking an unbounded discount. Omit for no cap.

usageLimit.description: How many times the coupon may be redeemed across the whole store -- 'the first 100 customers'. Omit for unlimited redemptions.

usageLimitPerUser.description: How many times one customer may redeem the coupon. Set 1 for the common 'one use per customer'. Omit for unlimited per customer.

id.description: The new coupon's id. Hand it to get_coupon to confirm the coupon persisted, and keep it for any later change.

code.description: The code customers type at checkout, as Salla stored it. Report this back to the merchant verbatim -- Salla may not preserve the exact casing that was sent.

type.description: 'fixed' or 'percentage', echoing how the discount is calculated.

status.description: The coupon's toggle as created: 'active' means customers can already redeem it once startDate has passed, 'inactive' means it exists but is switched off.

amount.description: The discount as Salla stored it. Note the asymmetry: a plain number was sent, but it comes back as a money object -- do not report this field as a bare number.

currency.description: ISO currency code of the store, e.g. 'SAR'.

maximum_amount.description: The cap on the discount, as a money object. An amount of 0 means no cap was set, not a coupon worth nothing.

currency.description: ISO currency code of the store.

expiry_date.description: When the coupon stops working, returned as 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' even though a plain date was sent.

start_date.description: When the coupon starts working, as 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS'. Null when no startDate was set, which means it is usable immediately.

free_shipping.description: Whether redeeming the coupon also makes the order ship free.

http.summary: Create Coupon -- create a single discount coupon. Salla's same endpoint also creates group and marketing coupons behind extra required field sets, which this tool deliberately does not expose.

fields.name: code
fields.description: The coupon code customers type at checkout.

fields.name: amount
fields.description: The discount value, as a plain number.

fields.name: expiry_date
fields.description: Last day the coupon works, YYYY-MM-DD.

fields.name: free_shipping
fields.description: Whether the coupon also gives free shipping.

fields.name: exclude_sale_products
fields.description: Whether products already on sale are excluded.

fields.name: start_date
fields.description: First day the coupon works, YYYY-MM-DD.

fields.name: minimum_amount
fields.description: Smallest order total the coupon applies to.

fields.name: maximum_amount
fields.description: Largest discount the coupon may take off.

fields.name: usage_limit
fields.description: Total redemptions allowed across the store.

statuses.meaning: The store's access token is missing, expired, or does not carry the marketing.read_write scope, so no coupon was created and the app's authorization has to be fixed first.

Salla rejected the coupon and created nothing -- usually a code that already exists in the store, or a required field missing or malformed. The top-level message is a translation key like 'alert.invalid_fields' and is not worth relaying; read error.fields, which names each bad field with a human reason, and tell the merchant which value to change.

rules.message: expiryDate must be a calendar date in YYYY-MM-DD form, e.g. 2026-12-31
startDate must be a calendar date in YYYY-MM-DD form, e.g. 2026-12-31

dependencies.reason: coupon codes must be unique in the store, so the agent should check the merchant's existing coupons with list_coupons before creating one that would be rejected as a duplicate
